posts.heading: November 8, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 25 species on this day, above the past week's average of 21.7, with 20 heard and 14 seen. Feeder visits came to 119, quieter than the week's average of 171.9, while detections (245) stayed close to the usual 241.6. Eastern Towhee led the heard list with 54 detections, and Tufted Titmouse (15) and Northern Cardinal (12) led the visits.

Brown-headed Cowbird returned after 8 days away, last recorded October 31, and Cedar Waxwing returned after 7 days, last recorded November 1. Twelve species were recorded on all seven of the prior days and this day, including American Crow, Blue Jay, Carolina Chickadee, Eastern Towhee, and Northern Cardinal. Snow Goose was recorded on this day for the first time in the past week.

The heard counts came from several microphones, switching among c120, pi, and pi-mic (movo-dom1). No species was heard for the first time at the station, and no first confident visual record was made.

posts.heading: November 7, 2026
posts.text:
November 7 added up to 22 species, with 20 heard, 12 seen and 10 both, across 61 feeder visits. Heard detections totaled 321, above the week's average of 246.6, while visits were the lowest of the eight days, tied with November 3 and well below the average of 189.6.

Twelve species were recorded on all seven days including this one, among them American Crow, Blue Jay, Carolina Chickadee, Northern Cardinal, Tufted Titmouse and White-throated Sparrow. Tufted Titmouse led the visits with 21 confident sightings, and the first visual of the day came 11 min before sunrise. The Eastern Bluebird returned after 15 days away, last recorded on October 23, and was heard once.

The audio source was switched many times during the day, moving between c120, pi and pi-mic (movo-dom1). No species was heard for the first time at the station, and no first confident visual record was set.

posts.heading: November 6, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to 22 species, 18 heard and 12 seen, across 113 feeder visits, which is below the past week's average of 195.4 visits and below its average of 259.6 heard detections. The species count matched the week's average of 21.9, and visits were higher than only two of the seven prior days. Tufted Titmouse led the visits with 47, and Eastern Towhee led the detections with 54.

Eleven species were recorded on all seven days, this one included, among them Eastern Towhee, Tufted Titmouse, Carolina Chickadee, Blue Jay and Northern Cardinal. Red-shouldered Hawk and American Goldfinch, which were recorded on five and four of the prior days, were not recorded today. Northern Cardinal was the first visual of the day at 24 min before sunrise and the last at 11 min after sunset.

The audio source changed many times through the day, moving between c120, pi and pi-mic (movo-dom1), so the heard counts came from whichever source was active at each point. No species was heard for the first time at this station today, and no first confident visual record was made. Hairy Woodpecker was heard once, at 15:00, and was recorded on three of the seven days, including this one.

posts.heading: November 5, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to 24 species, matching the high of the past week, with 211 feeder visits against a seven-day average of 185.9. Detections totaled 213 against a weekly average of 272.6, and of the 24 species, 19 were heard, 15 were seen, and 10 were both. Tufted Titmouse led the visits with 66 confident sightings, while Carolina Chickadee had 38 and White-breasted Nuthatch had 13.

Eastern Towhee and Carolina Chickadee led the detections with 43 and 40, and eleven species were recorded on all seven days, including this one. Canada Goose was back after 8 days away, last recorded 2026-10-28, and Palm Warbler was back after 27 days away, last recorded 2026-10-09. The first visual of the day was Northern Cardinal 10 min before sunrise, and the last was Mourning Dove 64 min before sunset. No species was seen at this station for the first time, and none was heard for the first time.

The audio source was switched many times during the day, among the pi, c120, and pi-mic (movo-dom1) microphones, with most changes in the early morning and late afternoon. Detections after each change came from the new source.

posts.heading: November 4, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to 24 species, 15 seen and 18 heard, with 279 feeder visits, well above the past week's average of 174.6 visits and the second-highest visit count of the eight days. Species count was also above the 21.6 average, while heard detections (130) ran well below the average of 300.6. Tufted Titmouse led the visits with 117 and Carolina Chickadee followed with 66, while Carolina Wren (19), Northern Cardinal (11) and House Finch (9) also made regular visits.

The Northern Flicker returned after 10 days away, last recorded on 2026-10-25, with one probable visual. Eleven species were recorded on all seven days, including today, and Red-shouldered Hawk and White-throated Sparrow were recorded on six of the seven. Northern Mockingbird and Red-bellied Woodpecker, both recorded on each of the previous seven days, were not recorded today.

There was no first confident visual record and no species heard for the first time at this station. The audio source changed repeatedly between 06:32 and 07:24 and again between 17:04 and 17:05. The first visual was a Carolina Chickadee 2 min before sunrise, and the last was a Carolina Wren 22 min before sunset.

posts.heading: November 3, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to 22 species, with 19 heard and 10 seen, 61 feeder visits, and 221 heard detections. That was quieter than the past week: visits sat well below the weekly average of 182.4, and detections were below the average of 322.9, while the species count of 22 was close to the average of 21.0. The first visual was a Chipping Sparrow 48 min after sunrise, and the last was a Carolina Chickadee 47 min before sunset.

All 13 species recorded on every day of the past week were present today, including Tufted Titmice with 22 confident visual visits and Carolina Chickadees with 14. White-throated Sparrow, recorded on 6 of the 7 days, was heard 30 times. Brown-headed Cowbird, Cedar Waxwing, Golden-crowned Kinglet, Gray Catbird, Common Grackle, and Hairy Woodpecker, which were recorded on other days of the week, were not recorded today.

No species was seen or heard for the first time at the station today. The audio source was changed many times throughout the day, beginning at 05:30 and continuing through 22:02, so heard detections came from more than one source. These changes are logged as the only station change for the day and do not by themselves account for the lower totals.

posts.heading: November 2, 2026
posts.text:
Across November 2, the station logged 17 species, 17 heard and 7 seen, with 75 feeder visits. That is below the seven-day average of 21.6 species and 196.3 visits, and detections of 290 sit below the average of 334.0. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees led the detections, with 61 and 59, and Tufted Titmice also led the visits with 30 confident sightings. Carolina Chickadee, Carolina Wren, Blue Jay, Northern Cardinal, and Eastern Phoebe were all recorded on each of the last seven days, including this one, while White-throated Sparrow, Brown-headed Cowbird, and Red-shouldered Hawk were not recorded today.

The station's audio source was switched many times over the past week, most heavily on October 27 and 28, and it also changed on this day, so detections from those periods come from different microphones. The day's first visual was a Carolina Chickadee and its last was a Carolina Wren. No species was heard here for the first time, and no first confident visual record was made.

The audio source changed repeatedly through the early morning of November 2, and the visit count on November 1 was 403, well above any other day in the window. Today's visit total of 75 came after that unusually busy day.
